title: Best Cloud Storage Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Tresorit, pCloud Crypto, Proton Drive and SpiderOak ONE compared on zero-knowledge encryption, free storage, platforms, sharing and business features.
intro: Most popular cloud storage services like Google Drive and Dropbox scan your files and can share data with third parties. Privacy-focused alternatives use zero-knowledge encryption to ensure only you can access your files, protecting against data breaches and surveillance.

products.name: Tresorit
products.tagline: Swiss zero-knowledge cloud storage with end-to-end encryption
products.pricing: Free 3GB Basic plan; paid plans from $4.75/month billed yearly (Personal Lite, 50GB)
pros: Based in Switzerland with strong privacy laws
Advanced sharing controls and access permissions
GDPR compliant with data residency options
Apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and web

products.name: Proton Drive
products.tagline: Encrypted cloud storage from the makers of Proton Mail
products.pricing: Free up to 5GB; Drive Plus (200GB) $4.99/month billed monthly
pros: Integrates with the Proton Mail ecosystem
End-to-end encryption included on the free 5GB plan
cons: Web interface could be more polished

products.name: pCloud Crypto
products.tagline: Affordable encrypted cloud storage with lifetime plans
products.pricing: Free up to 10GB; Crypto encryption add-on $49.99/year or $150 lifetime
cons: Encryption is a paid add-on, not built-in
Files in the encrypted Crypto folder can't be shared by link

products.name: SpiderOak ONE
products.tagline: No Knowledge privacy with continuous backup
pros: Zero-knowledge encryption when you use the desktop app
Version history and deleted file recovery
cons: No mobile apps: they were removed from the app stores
Signing in on the website gives up its zero-knowledge protection

verdict.summary: Tresorit scores highest here: end-to-end encryption by default, the most complete sharing controls and business features on this table, and apps for every major platform, though its free plan is only 3GB. pCloud Crypto and Proton Drive tie for second; pCloud Crypto is listed first only because ties are ordered alphabetically. pCloud gives you 10GB free, but its client-side encryption is a paid add-on and encrypted files can't be shared by link. Proton Drive includes encryption even on its free 5GB plan, but its business features are basic and it has no Linux desktop app yet. SpiderOak ONE scores lowest: it has no free plan and no mobile apps, and its web login gives up zero-knowledge protection. Sync speed isn't scored, because we haven't measured it.

bestFor.reason: Highest score here: advanced sharing controls, admin tools and end-to-end encryption
End-to-end encryption is included on the free 5GB plan; pCloud charges extra for its Crypto folder
One-time payment options for storage and the Crypto add-on, and 10GB of free storage
Continuous backup with version history and deleted-file recovery; use the desktop app, not the web login, to keep zero-knowledge protection

pro_tips: Where you can, use a provider's desktop or mobile app rather than its website: with some services, SpiderOak ONE for example, signing in on the web weakens the encryption.
Enable two-factor authentication on all cloud storage accounts, even encrypted ones, to add an extra layer of account protection.
Regularly audit shared files and folders to ensure you're not accidentally sharing sensitive data with unintended recipients.
Consider using different cloud providers for different types of data - one for regular files and another for highly sensitive documents.
Always verify that client-side encryption is properly enabled before uploading sensitive files, and test file recovery procedures regularly.

faqs.question: What is zero-knowledge encryption in cloud storage?
faqs.answer: Zero-knowledge encryption means your files are encrypted on your device before being uploaded to the cloud. The storage provider never has access to your encryption keys or unencrypted data, ensuring only you can read your files even if the provider is compromised or compelled to share data.

faqs.question: Are encrypted cloud storage services slower than regular ones?
faqs.answer: Encryption adds work on your device: files are encrypted before upload and decrypted after download, so large transfers can take a little longer. How much depends on your device, your connection and the service. This page doesn't score sync speed, because we haven't measured it.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Google Drive or Dropbox to an encrypted service?
faqs.answer: Yes, most encrypted cloud storage providers offer migration tools or detailed guides to help transfer your files. You can also manually download and re-upload files, though this takes longer for large amounts of data.

faqs.question: Do encrypted cloud storage services work offline?
faqs.answer: Yes, files stored locally through sync applications remain accessible offline. However, you need an internet connection to sync changes or access files that aren't stored locally on your device.

faqs.question: Are these services safe from government surveillance?
faqs.answer: Encrypted cloud storage with zero-knowledge architecture provides strong protection against surveillance since providers cannot decrypt your files even when compelled by authorities. However, metadata like file sizes and access patterns may still be visible, and local device security remains important.
